questions.q: What is the most professional initial response when an agitated customer returns to your workshop claiming their newly replaced touchscreen stopped working after just one day?
options: Refuse to interact with them until they leave the store and calm down.
Immediately blame the customer, insisting they must have dropped it in water.
Stay calm, listen actively, and offer to perform an immediate physical inspection of the device under warranty terms.
Process a full cash refund instantly without inspecting the actual device.
questions.explain: In good customer relations, active listening and offering a rapid physical inspection immediately de-escalate customer tension, while ensuring the business maintains protocol to check if the fault was due to defective parts or recent customer damage.

questions.q: While actively dismantling a smartphone for a quoted screen repair, you discover the primary logic board is snapped, doubling the initial estimated repair cost. In managing customer relations, what is the mandatory next step?
options: Complete the logic board repair silently and forcefully present the massively inflated final bill upon pickup.
Immediately halt all work, securely store the parts, and contact the client directly to explain the new damage and gain explicit authorization before proceeding.
Secretly install deeply inferior aftermarket components across the board to secretly match the initial financial estimate.
Immediately discard the repair ticket completely and hand the unassembled pieces back without verbal explanation.
questions.explain: Ethical transparency is foundational to avoiding major business disputes. Seeking explicit verbal or written authorization for unexpected cost increases respects the customer's budget constraints and ensures you get paid for the extra labor.
questions.exam: WASSCE Setting Up and Managing Mobile Phone Workshop

questions.q: To guarantee complete transparency and establish immense trust, what is unequivocally the most effective, professional final procedural step when physically returning a newly fixed smartphone back to the original owner?
options: Aggressively process the financial payment transaction and swiftly dismiss them to clear the store queue.
Physically invite the customer to independently execute a full operational test of all core functions on the device directly in front of the agent before exiting the premises.
Aggressively package the device in shrink wrap, seal it heavily, and command them to unbox and test it much later in private.
Secretly wipe all user photographs to establish absolute data privacy for the trip back home.
questions.explain: Forcing collaborative in-store device testing confirms immediate physical satisfaction, solidifies the technician's competence, and permanently squashes the "it wasn't working when I left the store" argument minutes after the client drives away.

questions.q: A corporate client desperately deposits a heavily saltwater-damaged high-end flagship phone for recovery, but militantly refuses to surrender the critical numerical unlock passcode, vehemently citing intense "data privacy/intellectual property" paranoia. To ruthlessly defend shop liability while appeasing quality constraints, how must the manager navigate this?
options: Instantly and aggressively permanently reject the hardware at the counter without absolute exception.
Overtly accept the job but secretly utilize specialized penetration extraction boxes to deeply bypass the passcodes against their exact stated demands.

Administratively force the executive client to legally sign an aggressive intake liability waiver stating the technical workshop absolutely cannot be sued for completely untested secondary components (biometrics, telephoto arrays) discovered failing upon device return.
Routinely brute-force numerical passcode variations manually until the OS permanently locks out.
questions.explain: Lacking passcode entry completely paralyses post-repair localized functional diagnostics (cameras, earpieces, touch matrices). Mandating a comprehensive liability waiver legally shields the technician from subsequent vicious false allegations asserting that "the shop suddenly broke my FaceID" when testing was impossible due to the client's own blockade.
